text.p: Men's Wearhouse Inc filed Thursday with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to sell up to 2.6 million common shares of stock.
The company said it will sell one million shares and 1.6 million shares will be sold by a group of shareholders including the company's chairman.
Underwriters for the offering, Bear Stearns & Co Inc, Morgan Stanley Dean Witter, PaineWebber Inc and Robertson Stephens & Co, have an over-allotment option of up to 390,000 shares.
The Houston-based retailer said it will use the estimated $30 million in proceeds to continue its expansion, which may include the acquisition of rival men's clothing retailer, Today's Man Inc.

In the SEC filing, the company said it has been in discussions with Today's Man creditors and other parties regarding a possible acquisition of more than a majority of Today's Man's 25 stores, an acquisition it estimates will cost $70 to $90 million.
Today's Man filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy early in 1996.
Despite its progress, Men's Wearhouse said the talks have not included Today's Man management and said any understanding between the company and creditors will likely be opposed by Today's Man.

"Due to the complexity of the situation and the conflicting goals of the several parties involved , there is a significant likelihood that the company may not be able to acquire the assets of Today's Man," the company said in the filing.
After the offering, Men's Wearhouse will have 22,026,576 common shares outstanding.
